notes: Formula Retail Employee Rights Ordinances (FRERO) cover chains with 40+ formula retail establishments worldwide and 20+ employees in San Francisco.
On-call employees not called in are owed 2 to 4 hours of pay.
No SF rest-between-shifts rule recorded; California state meal/rest/OT rules apply.

Predictability pay (L.E.C. § 42.4(c), OLSE FAQ § d): owed for each scheduled shift the employer moves or cancels, or each unscheduled shift the employer requires, with less than 7 days' notice: 1 h (notice >= 24 h, any length); under 24 h: 2 h if the hours added or subtracted are 4 or less, 4 h if more (under_24h_tiers). For a moved shift the FAQ does not say which hours count; engine should use the moved shift's hours (conservative). Schedules are posted 2 weeks ahead.

Exceptions (§ 42.4(e)): emergencies/utilities/Act of God closing operations; another scheduled employee unable to work due to illness, vacation or employer-provided time off (no 7 days' notice); another employee failed to report, was sent home or disciplined; mandatory overtime; employee shift trades or employee-requested changes. So covering an absent coworker owes no predictability pay regardless of consent; voluntariness alone is NOT an exemption: encoded voluntary_additional_hours_exempt=true with exemption_only_for_absent_coworker_hours=true (no consent form needed; open shifts or demand-driven call-ins still owe pay).
Coverage: formula retail establishments with 40+ establishments worldwide and 20+ employees in San Francisco (plus their janitorial/security contractors).

params.exemption_note: No pay owed when "Another Employee previously scheduled to work is unable to work due to illness, vacation, or employer-provided paid or unpaid time off" or failed to report; also for shift trades and employee-requested changes.

rules.summary: SF formula retail: for changes with less than 7 days' notice, 1 hour of pay (24 h+ notice) or 2/4 hours (under 24 h, change of up to/over 4 hours) at the regular rate. Covering for an absent or no-show coworker is exempt.
